# ztbrfs

> Provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution to a complex triangular band system of equations.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import ztbrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztbrfs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
ztbrfs(
    order,
    uplo, trans, diag,
    N, kd, nrhs,
    AB, LDAB,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'`, or `'conjugate-transpose'` |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | in |  | one of `'non-unit'`, `'unit'` | `'unit'` or `'non-unit'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kd ≥ 0` | number of super-/sub-diagonals |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array` | in | `kd + 1 × N` |  | triangular band matrix |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kd + 1`; row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `AB` (>= `kd+1`) |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of `B` |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of `X` |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output forward error bounds (length `nrhs`) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output backward error estimates (length `nrhs`) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | workspace (>= `2*N` complex elements); auto-allocated when `null` |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | workspace (>= `N` reals); auto-allocated when `null` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals or subdiagonals of the triangular band matrix A. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangular band matrix A, stored in the first kd+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: The solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
ztbrfs.ndarray(
    uplo, trans, diag,
    N, kd, nrhs,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → integer
```

Provides error bounds for the solution to a system with a complex triangular band matrix.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | specifies the operation type |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | specifies the operation type |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | in |  | one of `'non-unit'`, `'unit'` | specifies the operation type |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kd ≥ 0` | the number of superdiagonals or subdiagonals of the triangular band matrix A. |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | the number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array` | in | `kd + 1 × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AB` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `B` |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `X` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `X` |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `RWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `RWORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals or subdiagonals of the triangular band matrix A. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangular band matrix A, stored in the first kd+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: The solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import ztbrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztbrfs';

// Upper triangular band matrix, N=3, KD=1, NRHS=1:
const AB = new Complex128Array( [ 0, 0, 3, 0, 1, 1, 4, 1, 2, -1, 5, -1 ] );
const B = new Complex128Array( [ 4, 1, 6, 0, 5, -1 ] );
const X = new Complex128Array( [ 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0 ] );
const FERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const BERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 6 );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 3 );

const info = ztbrfs.ndarray( 'upper', 'no-transpose', 'non-unit', 3, 1, 1, AB, 1, 2, 0, B, 1, 3, 0, X, 1, 3, 0, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );
console.log( 'FERR:', FERR[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'BERR:', BERR[ 0 ] );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZTBRFS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZTBRFS provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution to a system of linear equations with a triangular band coefficient matrix.

The solution matrix X must be computed by ZTBTRS or some other means before entering this routine. ZTBRFS does not do iterative refinement because doing so cannot improve the backward error.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
